description: Shared comparison cases for the Python and Swift calculators. Rules: docs/comparison-rules.md.
rounding: ROUND_HALF_UP to two decimal places, ties away from zero, applied only to the rounded_fields
number_comparison: Results compare as canonical strings. A rounded field has exactly two fraction digits and a minus sign only when it is below zero, so -0.00 never appears. An exact field is plain decimal notation with no exponent, no trailing fractional zeros, no trailing point and no -0.

A year ending on February 29 against one ending on February 28: two full years whose ends are a day apart in month-day, so they compare and carry period_ends_differ (D82).
Apple-like 52-week years ending 2024-09-28 and 2025-09-27: full fiscal years a year apart whose ends differ by a day compare, with period_ends_differ set.
A 53-week year (371 days) after a 52-week year: the end moves six days later in month-day and still compares, with the flag.
A year ending on December 30 against the next ending on January 1: the ends sit two days apart across the new year, so they compare.
Equal year-end month-days keep the calendar-year path and carry no flag.
Ends 2024-09-28 and 2025-10-10: both look like full years, but the later end is twelve days past the anniversary, so it refuses.
Two full years whose ends are 357 days apart: the later end falls eight days before the anniversary, past the seven-day limit.
A half year against a full fiscal year whose end differs by a day: the half year is not a full fiscal year, so it refuses.
Two 52-week years with a year between them: the ends are two years apart, so it refuses as a period-end mismatch.
A 53-week year that starts before the prior 52-week year ends: the periods share days, so neither is a baseline.
